question.text: What is the concept of 'Periodic Updation of KYC' and why is it important?

answer.text: Regularly refreshing customer identification data and risk profiles to ensure information remains current and accurate
Asking customers to submit new KYC documents every month
Updating KYC records only when the customer makes a complaint
Periodically deleting old KYC records to free up storage space

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook requires periodic updation of client and beneficial-owner documents, data and information so that CDD information remains up to date and relevant. Updation frequency is risk-based, with higher-risk clients requiring regular KYC-profile updates to keep the institution's risk view accurate. The Trap: Monthly resubmission is excessive and not the regulatory standard; complaint-driven or storage-driven updates miss the point — the rule is risk-based periodic refresh, not event-driven cleanup. Note: The workbook describes the obligation in qualitative, risk-based terms ("up to date and relevant", "regular KYC-profile updates" for higher-risk clients) rather than fixed annual or multi-year intervals.
